newsitem.title: USA: Fed seen refraining from open market operations.
newsitem.headline: Fed seen refraining from open market operations.

text.p: The Federal Reserve Bank of New York is expected to refrain from money market operations on Tuesday, analysts said.
"With the (federal) funds trading below target, the Fed will probably stay out today," said Dana Saporta, economist at Stone and McCarthy Research Associates Inc.
Saporta said she sees the Fed's daily average add need at about $2.0 billion in the remaining two days of the current two-week reserve maintenance period.
"But it looks like the Fed can clean that up by the end of the period tomorrow," Saporta said.
Analysts at consulting firm MMS International Inc also expect the Fed to stay out of the market on Tuesday.
At 0950 EDT/1350 GMT, the federal funds rate stood at 5-3/16 percent, below the Fed's 5-1/4 percent target.
